items.title: Associative emotional memory encoding: insights from network stability analysis of an fMRI-driven bilinear dynamics
items.summary: Objectives The interplay between emotion and memory is a central topic in cognitive neuroscience, with open questions about the underlying neuronal mechanisms. This article aims to study the effects of order and intensity of emotional information on associative memory encoding. To this aim, we employ dynamic causal modeling to model the dynamic network composed of the hippocampus, amygdala, and orbitofrontal cortex during an fMRI associative memory encoding task and apply graph and control theory tools to obtain novel insights. items.title: Graph Neural Networks in Network Neuroscience
items.summary: This paper explores the application of Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) in Network Neuroscience for analyzing brain connectivity patterns derived from neuroimaging data such as fMRI, EEG, and DTI. The study discusses Graph Convolutional Networks (GCNs), Graph Attention Networks (GATs), brain network modeling, neurological disorder detection, and future research directions in AI-driven neuroscience.

items.title: The Weighted Sequence
items.summary: Contemporary B2B marketing has accelerated itself into a structural contradiction. Outreach sequences, automation platforms, and multichannel digital programmes have grown faster and more sophisticated, while purchasing decisions in complex B2B environments have simultaneously slowed, distributed across buying committees of unprecedented size, and moved substantially into the pre-commercial period that precedes any vendor contact. items.title: Brainana: an end-to-end preprocessing framework for macaque neuroimaging
items.summary: Macaque MRI bridges non-invasive systems neuroscience with cellular and circuit-level mechanisms, but preprocessing remains fragmented across tools that are difficult to integrate, adapt to non-human primate acquisitions, and deploy reproducibly. We present Brainana, an automated, BIDS-compatible preprocessing framework for macaque neuroimaging. items.title: Emotion Representation and Neural Synchrony: Decoding Valence and Arousal with Wearable EEG
items.summary: Emotions are dynamic experiences that unfold over time, yet most affective neuroscience studies have relied on static stimuli and laboratory-based EEG systems. items.title: FieldTrip: Open Source Software for Advanced Analysis of MEG, EEG, and Invasive Electrophysiological Data
items.summary: This paper describes FieldTrip, an open source software package that we developed for the analysis of MEG, EEG, and other electrophysiological data. The software is implemented as a MATLAB toolbox and includes a complete set of consistent and user-friendly high-level functions that allow experimental neuroscientists to analyze experimental data. It includes algorithms for simple and advanced analysis, such as time-frequency analysis using multitapers, source reconstruction using dipoles, distributed sources and beamformers, connectivity analysis, and nonparametric statistical permutation tests

items.title: Image processing with ImageJ
items.summary: Wayne Rasband of NIH has created ImageJ, an open source Java-written program that is now at version 1.31 and is used for many imaging applications, including those that that span the gamut from skin analysis to neuroscience. ImageJ is in the public domain and runs on any operating system (OS). ImageJ is easy to use and can do many imaging manipulations. A very large and knowledgeable group makes up the user community for ImageJ.
